# DBeaver interop fixtures

Synthetic DBeaver workspaces used by the `ninesql-dbeaver` tests (ROADMAP P0-E, consumed by P2-A).

The **file format is genuine**: each workspace was written by a real DBeaver Community Edition build. The **content is 100 % fake**: hosts under `.invalid`, made-up users, passwords made up for the tests. Real DBeaver workspaces are never committed (see `.gitignore` and [AGENTS.md](../../../../AGENTS.md)).

DBeaver is only a test-data generator. It is downloaded outside the repository, never linked and never committed (invariant I7).

## Layout

Each fixture keeps DBeaver's relative layout of a default Linux workspace (`~/.local/share/DBeaverData/workspace6/`):

```
dbeaver-<version>/workspace6/
├── .metadata/dbeaver-workspace.properties   only the product-name / product-version lines
└── General/
    ├── .project                             Eclipse project file with the DBeaver nature
    └── .dbeaver/
        ├── data-sources.json                connections, folders, connection types (plain JSON)
        └── credentials-config.json          saved users / passwords (encrypted, see below)
```

Only the files NineSQL reads are copied. Left out: `.metadata/.plugins/`, logs, `dbeaver-instance.properties` (local port), `workspace-id`, `General/.settings/`, and the `.data-sources.json.bak` / `.credentials-config.json.bak` backups DBeaver writes next to the real files (an importer must ignore these dot-files). DBeaver did not create `project-settings.json` or `Scripts/` in these flows, so they are not covered yet.

## Connections (identical in every version)

Connection ids are generated by DBeaver (`<driver-id>-<hex>-<hex>`) and differ per version: tests must look connections up by `name`.

| Name | Provider / driver | Covers | Connection type | Saved credentials | Generated vs hand-edited |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `pg-dev` | `postgresql` / `postgres-jdbc` | folder `Team A`, driver properties (`ApplicationName`, `connectTimeout`), bootstrap default schema + init query | `dev` | user + password | `-con`; bootstrap hand-edited |
| `pg-prod-ssh` | `postgresql` / `postgres-jdbc` | nested folder `Team A/Production`, read-only flag, SSH tunnel with password auth | `prod` | user + password, SSH user + password | `-con`; type, read-only and SSH hand-edited |
| `pg-url-tls` | `postgresql` / `postgres-jdbc` | JDBC URL only (no host / port), TLS handler `postgre_ssl` verify-full with CA / client cert / key paths | `dev` | user only (password not saved) | `-con`; TLS hand-edited |
| `timescale-metrics` | `postgresql` / `postgres-timescale-jdbc` | TimescaleDB driver of the PostgreSQL provider | `dev` | user + password | `-con` |
| `mysql-test` | `mysql` / `mysql8` | manual commit (`bootstrap.autocommit = false`), driver properties | `test` | user + password | `-con`; type hand-edited |
| `mariadb-ssh-key` | `mysql` / `mariaDB` | no folder, SSH tunnel with public key (key path, saved passphrase), TLS handler `mysql_ssl` that does **not** verify the server certificate | `dev` | user only, SSH user + passphrase | `-con`; SSH and TLS hand-edited |
| `sqlite-local` | `sqlite` / `sqlite_jdbc` | file database (fake path `/home/nine_user/data/fixture.sqlite`), connection description | `dev` | none | `-con`; description hand-edited |
| `clickhouse-analytics` | `clickhouse` / `com_clickhouse` | v0.2 engine, custom connection type | `staging` (custom) | user + password | `-con`; type hand-edited |
| `oracle-legacy` | `oracle` / `oracle_thin` | engine outside the v1 set (must be imported disabled) | `dev` | user + password | `-con` |
| `roundtrip-marker` | `postgresql` / `postgres-jdbc` | added by the second DBeaver run to force re-serialization (see below) | `dev` | user only | `-con` |

Folders: `Team A` (with a description, hand-edited), `Team A/Production`, `Team B`, `Analytics`, `Legacy`.
Connection types present: `dev`, `prod`, `test` (DBeaver built-ins, written by DBeaver itself) and `staging` (custom, hand-edited).

## `credentials-config.json` encryption

Verified on all five versions (same scheme, same decrypted structure):

- AES-128-CBC with PKCS#5/7 padding.
- Key: the fixed key from DBeaver Community's source code, hex `babb4a9f774ab853c96c2d653dfe544a` (identical for every installation; that is why NineSQL moves the secrets to the keyring, ADR-0005).
- File = 16-byte IV followed by the ciphertext.
- Plaintext: compact JSON, `{ "<connection id>": { "#connection": { "user": …, "password": … }, "network/ssh_tunnel": { "user": …, "password": … } } }`. Keys are omitted when no value is saved; connections with nothing saved have no entry.

Decrypted values are for tests only and must stay in memory (I1); never print them in test output or snapshots.

## How the fixtures were generated

Run on Ubuntu 24.04 (x86_64) with `xvfb`, `xdotool`, `xauth` and the GTK 3 runtime (`libgtk-3-0t64`) installed through `apt-get`. For each version:

```sh
# outside the repository, one new empty directory per version
mkdir -p "$SCRATCH/$VERSION" && tar -xzf "dbeaver-ce-$VERSION-<suffix>.tar.gz" -C "$SCRATCH/$VERSION"
crates/ninesql-dbeaver/tests/fixtures/generate.sh "$VERSION" "$SCRATCH/$VERSION/dbeaver" \
  "$SCRATCH/run-$VERSION" crates/ninesql-dbeaver/tests/fixtures/dbeaver-$VERSION
```

[`generate.sh`](generate.sh) does the following:

1. Starts DBeaver under `Xvfb` with a fresh workspace (`-data`), a throw-away `HOME`, `-Duser.name=nine_user`, no proxy variables (DBeaver gets no network access), and one `-con "driver=…|name=…|…|save=true|connect=false"` per connection, plus `-quit`. First-run dialogs (sample database, tips) are dismissed with `xdotool`. On 26.x the first-run "Product Configuration" wizard is suppressed with `-Dproduct.config.disable=true`.
2. Applies [`hand-edit.py`](hand-edit.py) to `data-sources.json` (see below).
3. Starts DBeaver again with one more `-con` (`roundtrip-marker`). Saving it makes DBeaver re-read the hand-edited file and re-serialize **the whole registry** in its own format: plaintext handler credentials are moved into `credentials-config.json`, connection-type definitions are rewritten from DBeaver's own registry, and anything DBeaver does not understand is dropped. The committed files are this second output, so every field in them was written by DBeaver.
4. Copies the files listed under [Layout](#layout).

DBeaver 25.x and 26.x exit on their own after `-quit`; 22.x to 24.x do not when started headless, so the script stops them with `SIGTERM` once the expected connections are on disk (DBeaver writes both files synchronously when a connection is saved; the script checks the connection count after exit).

### Hand edits

DBeaver's `-con` option cannot set the connection type, the read-only flag, descriptions, bootstrap queries, or network handlers in any of these versions: its `handler.<id>.<prop>` parameters are only used to match an existing connection, never applied to a new one (checked in DBeaver's `DataSourceUtils` for each version). `hand-edit.py` therefore adds, in DBeaver's JSON structure and matched by connection name:

- folder description on `Team A`;
- custom connection type `staging` (name, color, description, auto-commit, confirmations);
- `pg-dev`: `bootstrap.defaultSchema` and `bootstrap.query` (DBeaver's key for init queries);
- `pg-prod-ssh`: `read-only: true`, `configuration.type = "prod"`, `handlers.ssh_tunnel` (password auth) with `user` / `password` in the handler object;
- `pg-url-tls`: `handlers.postgre_ssl` (`sslMode`, `ssl.method`, certificate paths);
- `mysql-test`: `configuration.type = "test"`;
- `mariadb-ssh-key`: `handlers.ssh_tunnel` (`PUBLIC_KEY`, `keyPath`, passphrase as `password`) and `handlers.mysql_ssl` (`ssl.require`, `ssl.verify.server = false`, …);
- `sqlite-local`: `description`;
- `clickhouse-analytics`: `configuration.type = "staging"`.

Caveats of the hand edits (to verify against UI-created workspaces before the importer relies on them):

- Handler property values are written as strings (`"port": "22"`). When given JSON numbers, DBeaver re-serializes them as floats (`22.0`); what the DBeaver UI itself writes is not verified here, so the parser must accept strings, integers and floats.
- `ssl.method` / handler property names come from DBeaver's classes, not from a UI-created file.

## Format differences observed between versions

Useful for P2-A (the parser must accept all of them):

| Area | 22.3.5 | 23.3.5 / 24.3.5 / 25.3.5 | 26.2.4 |
|---|---|---|---|
| Connection-type keys | `name`, `color`, `description`, `auto-commit`, `confirm-execute`, `confirm-data-change`, `auto-close-transactions` | adds `smart-commit`, `smart-commit-recover`, `close-transactions-period`, `auto-close-connections`, `close-connections-period` | adds `colorDark` and `security.permission-restrictions` (array) |
| Built-in type colors | `prod` / `test` color is a theme key (`org.jkiss.dbeaver.color.connectionType.prod.background`); `dev` is `255,255,255` | same as 22.3.5 | plain `R,G,B` (`250,207,207` prod, `214,250,207` test) plus `colorDark` |
| `configuration.closeIdleConnection` | absent | `true` on every connection | absent again |
| Default values of built-in types | `auto-close-transactions` false for dev / test | periods differ between 23.3.5 and 24.3.5 (e.g. dev `close-connections-period` 3600 then 14400) | same as 25.3.5 |
| Nested folders | `"Production": { "parent": "Team A" }` | same | `"Team A/Production": {}` (full path as the key, no `parent`) for a folder created from `-con folder=Team A/Production`; UI-created nested folders not verified |
| `credentials-config.json` | AES-128-CBC, fixed key, IV prefix | same | same |
| `dbeaver-workspace.properties` | `product-version` in the workspace `.metadata` | same (25.3.5 with `-data` wrote it to the default `HOME` location instead; the script merges both) | same as 22.3.5 |

Stable in all versions: top-level `folders` / `connections` / `connection-types`; connection keys `provider`, `driver`, `name`, `save-password`, `read-only`, `folder`, `description`, `configuration` (`host`, `port` as a string, `database`, `url`, `configurationType: "MANUAL"`, `type`, `properties`, `bootstrap`, `handlers`); handler keys `type` (`TUNNEL` / `CONFIG`), `enabled`, `save-password`, `properties`; JDBC URLs escape `=` as `=` (Gson).

## Anonymization check

All values were chosen fake before generation, so nothing needed scrubbing. The committed files were checked for: the build machine's host name, `root`, `/root`, `/tmp/`, `localhost`, `127.0.0.1` and real-looking hosts (none found). The only absolute paths are the made-up `/home/nine_user/...` paths written on purpose. `tests/fixtures_layout.rs` re-checks hosts and forbidden strings on every test run.

Note for anyone regenerating: DBeaver writes the full `-con` command line, passwords included, to its own `.metadata/.log` and to `configuration/*.log` in the install directory. Those files stay in the scratch directory and are never copied here; this is one more reason to only ever use fake values.
